cards.title: One idea behind many tricks
cards.body:
Subtracting 1 flips the lowest set bit and every bit below it: `12 = 1100`, `11 = 1011`. So `x & (x - 1)` **clears the lowest set bit**: `1100 & 1011 = 1000`.

- Power of two? It has exactly one set bit, so clearing it gives 0.
- Count bits: clear the lowest bit until nothing is left.
- Flags: give each property (wild, scatter, sticky) one bit of an `unsigned`.
The tests compare these against C++20's `<bit>` functions (`std::popcount`, `std::has_single_bit`) on 1,000 random numbers.

cards.question: What is `40 & 39`?
cards.explain: 40 = 101000, 39 = 100111. AND keeps only the shared top bit: 100000 = 32. (40 isn't a power of two, so the result isn't 0.)

cards.question: flags = 0b0101. Is bit 2 set?
cards.explain: (0b0101 >> 2) & 1 = 0b01 & 1 = 1. Bits are numbered from 0 on the right.
